title: Great God, I Own Thy Sentence Just
description: Great God, I Own Thy Sentence Just in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 6, headed “Triumph over death, Job 19. 25-27”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Great God, I own thy sen-tence just And na-ture must de-cay; I yield my bo-dy to the dust To dwell with fel-low clay.

lines: Great God, I own thy sentence just
I yield my body to the dust
Yet faith may triumph o'er the grave,
And Death, the last of all his foes,
Tho' greedy worms devour my skin,
When God shall build my bones again,
Then shall I see thy lovely face
And feast upon thy unknown grace

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
